about: Alpe is a small distillery in Hône, at the mouth of the Champorcher valley in Italy’s Valle d’Aosta, the mountain region bordering France and Switzerland. It has worked for more than fifty years in the manner of the old Aostan distilleries, producing in small quantities and using no artificial flavourings or colours. Génépy is its flagship, alongside grappas and herbal liqueurs.

The liqueur is named for the Herbetet, a peak in the Gran Paradiso massif, where the génépy wormwoods grow on glacial moraines above 2,000 metres. Artemisia genipi and Artemisia mutellina lead, with oregano, mint and cinnamon. The herbs are picked in August, dried and steeped in a wheat spirit for about a month; part of the infusion is redistilled, and it is sweetened with beet sugar.

The importer notes earthy génépy, mint, clove and lemon peel on the nose, a rooty, herbal palate with marjoram and sandalwood, and a warming finish of pine, cinnamon and ripe berries. In the valley it is the traditional digestivo, taken slightly chilled after a heavy mountain meal, and it also works as a bright, herbal accent in cocktails.
